title: Data on Victim and Perpetrator Profiles in Rape and Molest Cases
what_it_is: Data on Victim and Perpetrator Profiles in Rape and Molest Cases

sections.label: Sexual offence cases and locations
sections.summary: Rape and outrage of modesty cases rose from 2024 to 2025, mostly involving known offenders, with offences occurring in residential, commercial and educational premises.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: From 2024 to 2025, there was an increase of 104 cases of outrage of modesty, from 1,427 to 1,531 cases; and an increase of 78 cases of rape, from 401 to 479 cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The majority of the rape cases and more than half of the outrage of modesty cases involved offenders known to the victims.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The proportions of rape and outrage of modesty cases involving offenders known to the victims has remained stable over the last five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: In 2025, of the total number of rape and outrage of modesty cases, approximately 33% took place in residential premises, 18% took place in commercial premises and 3% took place in educational institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Coordinating Minister for National Security and Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Government takes a firm stance against all forms of sexual offending and Ministries have implemented a suite of measures to prevent offending, encourage reporting and improve victim support, regardless of where the offence occurs.
